_comment: Maintained by Claude — see ../CLAUDE.md 'Dashboard Maintenance' rule. Status values: concept | in-progress | review | ready | archived. Keys in 'mocks' are folder paths relative to products/Scheduling/ (no trailing /index.html).

recentChanges.summary: Existing-assignment flow (Flow B): the Create New Assignment Template flow is no longer a separate 'Select Qualifiers' modal — the qualifier picker is now an inline panel under 'Assignment Template(s)' inside the Select Assignment(s) modal, revealed by the '+ Create New Assignment Template' trigger (Cancel/Create inline; trigger hides while creating or once a template exists). Also: open slots in the deployment result on the form are now clickable and open the Select Employee people picker (flowB) to fill the position in place.

Flow Map node badges reworked: comment-widget comments now show as the prominent 💬 emoji badge in the node's top-right corner; dev annotations moved out of the corner to a purple glassmorphism badge (Font Awesome note icon) next to the step label. Removed the hover magnifying (node scale-up) on the map. Renamed the two multi-assignment branch nodes to their triggering action — Branch A 'Click an assignment' (clicking an open slot on any assignment, not a template, in the Select Assignment(s) modal → employee picker) and Branch B '+ Create New Assignment Template' (opens the Select Qualifiers dialog).

Toolbox: the comment-mode banner ('Click any element to leave feedback') now floats just above the bottom-center toolbox dock instead of top-right, and drops its redundant 'Esc to cancel' button — the docked Comments button already becomes ✕ Cancel in pick mode (Esc still works). Comment widget bumped to 1.16.1 (designtoolbox/feedback-widget.js change).

Toolbox: comment-widget button + Flow Map button now share one bottom-center 'version switcher' dock (window.ToolboxDock, defined in designtoolbox/toolbox.js) instead of a floating top-right bubble + separate pill — only affects mocks that load toolbox.js (deployment). Also replaced the Flow Map's localStorage dev annotations with read-only dev notes loaded from a committed DEV-NOTES.md next to the mock (shared via git, no longer per-browser); added deployment/DEV-NOTES.md with per-step developer handoff notes and made the flow-map drawer read-only with 📝 badge counts sourced from that file. Comment widget bumped to 1.16.0.

Moved the Flow Map launcher out of the bottom-right corner into a bottom-center version-switcher pill; on a single-version mock like deployment the switcher shows just the Flow Map button (shared designtoolbox/flow-map.js change).

Create New Deployment now starts with an empty qualifiers panel (removed the seeded FF/Capt/PM default; clears on every 'Add New Deployment'), and replaced the static start/end clock boxes with real vaadin-time-picker time inputs alongside the date pickers.

Renamed the toolbox folder to lowercase designtoolbox/ and updated every reference (12 mock embeds, widget internals, READMEs, the deployment loader include). Fixed a flow-map bug where the 'Flow Map' launcher button only mounted when the map was opened programmatically — it now mounts on page load, so the toolbox + flow map are fully applied to the deployment mock.

Consolidated the design tools into a single root designtoolbox/ folder (the comment widget — feedback-widget.js, log.html, worker/, scripts/ — plus the flow map: toolbox.js, flow-map.js, flow-thumbs/). Moved flow-thumbs out of deployment/. Repointed all comment-widget embeds across 12 mocks to ../../../designtoolbox/feedback-widget.js, updated the widget's internal log URL + inject script, and pointed the deployment loader at ../../../designtoolbox/toolbox.js. toolbox.js now loads both the widget and flow map relative to itself (also fixes an absolute-path bug that broke the comment-widget injection on GitHub Pages).

Extracted the flow map into a reusable Design Toolbox drop-in (Toolbox/toolbox.js + flow-map.js) that adds the comment widget + flow map to any mock via one include and a window.TOOLBOX_CONFIG. Thumbnails are now LIVE — each node renders the mock itself at that state in a scaled iframe (booted via #fm=<state>), so they auto-update when the design changes instead of using static Figma PNGs. Added per-node dev annotations for developers (localStorage, add/edit/delete with a 📝 badge) and per-step comment-count chips (💬) inferred from the feedback widget's pins, with click-to-view. Deployment is the first consumer (exposes window.applyFlowState + hash boot).

Deployment refinements: relabeled the deployment-type radio to 'Create from scratch' vs 'Select existing assignments'; gated the Select Assignment(s) button behind required start/end dates (employees pre-populate from who's scheduled on the start date); added an 'Is Deployable?' toggle column to the Edit Assignments table so only deployable assignments appear in the selection modal; the Select Employee picker now ranks recommended (full primary+shared match) first then partial matches; assigned people can be removed/replaced via an X on filled slots in both flows; and added messaging that open slots aren't required to deploy (can be filled later via callback).

Built the Edit Assignments landing page (production chrome: dark top nav, Crew Scheduling sidebar, ACTIVE/ARCHIVED tabs, full assignments table with Edit/Delete) as the shared entry point. 'Add New Deployment' opens the Create New Deployment form, which now branches: 'Create Deployment' = Flow A (qualifiers panel), 'Select Existing Assignments' = Flow B. Built out Flow B end to end — Select Assignment(s) modal with selectable assignment cards and teal slot bars, the Select Employee picker on open slots, and the Create New Assignment Template (Select Qualifiers) dialog, ending in the filled deployment. Made the Create New Deployment form full-page width (no floating card). Reproduced from Figma and verified with Playwright. Flow Map gained an Edit Assignments entry node that branches into both flows, and all Flow B nodes now deep-link into live states.

Flow Map nodes now deep-link into the live prototype: clicking a built (Create Deployment) screen drives the real form into that exact state — empty form, qualifiers added, Select Employee picker open, or all slots filled — as if the user had clicked their way there, skipping the intermediate steps. Multi-Assignment screens (not built yet) keep the static image preview as a fallback, with a clear hover hint distinguishing live vs. preview nodes.

Added a 'Flow Map' dev/admin tool: a floating map button opens a pannable, zoomable map of every branching design flow (Create Deployment + Multi-Assignment) using Figma screen grabs as thumbnails. Hovering a screen swells it and reveals its description; clicking opens that screen full screen with prev/next navigation. Thumbnails stored under deployment/flow-thumbs/.

Created the Create Deployment (single) flow from Figma: the Create New Deployment form (details, color, effective dates, work types, notes) plus an interactive qualifiers panel — adding primary/shared qualifiers with steppers generates open position slots, and clicking an open slot opens a Select Employee dialog that fills the slot.

Rule builder no longer skips follow-up sub-questions implied by an answer. For the two reset-based rules (Accumulation — Hours Based, Accumulating Rolodex), picking an option like 'Custom mix', 'Custom range', 'Both, weighted', or a 'Custom' limit now inserts the detail question it implies (e.g. which outcomes, what range, how to weight, what limit) before resuming the main flow exactly where it left off. Main question order is unchanged.

Applied AI-branding feedback: swapped the single-star sparkle for the company-standard 3-star AI icon everywhere it appears (~18 spots — AI assistant avatar, badges, Add New Rule button, empty states, etc.), and added the company-approved 'Powered by AI' phrasing to the rule-builder header and the AI Assistant card header.

Made the flow switcher auto-hide and reveal macOS Dock–style: it's tucked off the bottom edge by default (a faint grabber hints at it) and slides up when the user hovers or clicks the bottom-center reveal strip, then slides away shortly after the pointer leaves.

Expanded the bottom-center flow switcher from two options to three and relabeled them. New front/default 'Rules engine' flow lands the user straight inside the dual-screen rule builder (as if Add New Rule was just clicked). 'First setup' (was V1) is the fresh no-approaches onboarding, and 'Rule step' (was V2) is the approaches-created/create-first-rule state.

Fixed the guided rule-builder asking for approaches twice: now that approaches are the opening question, picking a ranking template (e.g. 'Accumulation — Hours Based') no longer re-asks 'Which approach(es) should this rule cover?' as the template's first question. The template's approaches step is skipped, its rule-intro line is grafted onto the next real question, and an 'Applies to: …' chip confirms the approaches already chosen. The duplicate is only suppressed when approaches were already answered (guided/seeded) — the describe-it-yourself and MOU paths still ask approaches normally.

In the rule builder's 'Describe it in my own words' path, the prepopulated starting-point suggestions are no longer shown up front — the user is prompted to write their own description first (with the spotlighted text box), and the suggestions appear only after they've written and sent that first description.

deployment.title: Deployments
deployment.description: End-to-end Deployments prototype imported from Figma. Starts on the Edit Assignments landing (production chrome); 'Add New Deployment' opens the full-page Create New Deployment form, which branches into Flow A (Create Deployment — interactive qualifiers panel + open-slot Select Employee picker) or Flow B (Select Existing Assignments — Select Assignment(s) modal, slot bars, and Create Assignment Template dialog). Includes a 'Flow Map' dev tool: a branching map of every screen with an Edit Assignments entry node, hover-preview, and click-to-open-live deep-linking into both flows.

Event Indicator UX-2474.description: Rethinking how events are grouped and indicated on the scheduling calendar. Includes a 'Current UI' companion page (current-ui.html) reproducing the live production day view as the 'before' comparison.

Rules engine only.description: Standalone rules engine view for configuring scheduling automations and constraints.
